title: Security Policy
text: Report security issues using GitHub’s private vulnerability reporting feature. Click “Report vulnerability” Security Advisories tab. open public issue report email, Slack, channel. report received securely, kept confidential, routed right people. See GitHub’s documentation process works. Note: HHS VDP also accepts reports hhs.responsibledisclosure.com. vulnerabilities repository NIH systems hosted , use GitHub report link responsible team notified directly. Please include: - vulnerability potential impact - found - Steps reproduce (proof--concept scripts screenshots helpful)

title: Security Policy
text: Issued HHS VDP — Authorization. Good faith research conducted policy authorized. NIH HHS work resolve issues quickly pursue legal action related research.

title: Security Policy
text: Issued HHS VDP — Guidelines. Authorized research means : Notify us soon possible discovering real potential security issue Avoid privacy violations, user experience degradation, production system disruption, data destruction manipulation Use exploits extent necessary confirm vulnerability — exfiltrate data, establish access persistence, pivot systems Allow reasonable amount time resolve issue public disclosure compromise privacy, safety, intellectual property, financial interests HHS/NIH personnel third parties discover vulnerability encounter sensitive data (PII, financial, proprietary, trade secrets), stop testing, report immediately via GitHub private vulnerability report, disclose data anyone else.

title: Security Policy
text: Issued HHS VDP — Scope. nih.gov subdomains scope. Vendor systems scope — report vendor directly. Unsure system scope? Contact support@responsibledisclosure.com testing.

title: Security Policy
text: Issued HHS VDP — Rules Engagement. Must : - Test systems outside scope - Disclose vulnerability information except described policy - Conduct physical testing, social engineering, phishing - Execute denial--service resource exhaustion attacks - Introduce malicious software - Degrade, impair, disrupt, disable HHS/NIH systems - Test third-party applications services integrate NIH systems - Delete, alter, share, retain, destroy, exfiltrate HHS/NIH data - Use exploit establish access, persistence, pivot systems May: - View store NIH nonpublic data necessary document potential vulnerability Must: - Cease testing immediately report vulnerability nonpublic data exposure via GitHub private vulnerability report - Purge stored NIH nonpublic data upon reporting

title: Security Policy
text: Issued HHS VDP — Disclosure. share details discovered vulnerabilities 90 calendar days receiving acknowledgment. believe earlier disclosure warranted, coordinate us advance. text: Messier, Kyle (NIH/NIEHS) kyle.messier@nih.gov project maps concentrations hazardous air pollutants (HAPs) fine resolution across United States recent years (2018-2021). utilize multivariate, penalized, land-use-regression model spatiotemporally correlated errors simultaneously model several HAPs interest, using HAPs data EPA’s Ambient Monitoring Archive covariate data several atmospheric, meteorological, land cover, emissions variables, among others. use Multivariate Matern Gaussian Process modeling coupled General Vecchia approximation, enabling simultaneous variable selection LUR estimation fixed random effects large number variables. Additionally, employ state---art analysis pipelines ensuring model results reproducible tested.
